record.original_question: Constructive mathematics is mathematics together with the assumption that existence equals computability. Study constructive constructions and objects from the viewpoint of program-size complexity, not only from the viewpoint of dynamic complexities.

evidence.quote: Constructive mathematics is essentially mathematics plus the assumption that "existence = computability". Constructions and objects in constructive mathematics have been studied from the point of view of dynamic complexities and it would be interesting to study them also from the point of view of program-size complexity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Constructive mathematics may be described as ordinary mathematics together with the principle that "existence equals computability"; that is, every existence proof must yield an algorithm producing the asserted object. For a partial computable function U: {0,1}* → {0,1}* (a universal description method), the program-size (Kolmogorov) complexity of a finite object x is K_U(x) = min{ |p| : U(p) = x }, and analogous notions are defined for computable infinite objects via prefixes or via indices for total computable functions. Dynamic (time/space) complexity of constructive objects and constructions has been extensively investigated; by contrast, develop a systematic study of constructive mathematics from the viewpoint of program-size complexity. Concretely:

(a) For standard constructive objects (e.g., computable real numbers, computable metric spaces, computable continuous functions, Bishop-style constructions), define and analyze the program-size complexity of natural representatives, and establish nontrivial upper and lower bounds.

(b) For canonical constructive theorems (e.g., constructive versions of the intermediate value theorem, fixed-point theorems, completeness arguments), bound the program-size complexity of the witnesses produced by their proofs in terms of the complexities of the inputs.

(c) Identify a precise sense in which program-size complexity yields qualitative or quantitative information about constructive proofs that is not captured by time- or space-complexity measures.

The task is to carry out this program with theorems giving such bounds and structural results.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this broad research program was located. It is phrased as a long-term direction rather than a single conjecture, and no source was found announcing that constructive mathematics has been comprehensively analyzed from the program-size complexity viewpoint. Status is therefore taken as unknown.
